refuted.claim: Title + opening: 'Institutional — the channel that earns nothing, and should not be grown'; 'ARY's institutional business is Rs 69.81 lakh of revenue producing Rs 0.72 lakh of gross profit'; conclusion 'Do not grow this channel' and 'institutional supply is no longer on the list'
refuted.why: The note equates 'institutional' with ONE customer (Hunger Heroes, a Delhi NGO) while its own Rs 51.25 L ten-account campus table sits three sections below. I re-ran the note's exact WAC method per campus account: EVERY ONE of the ten earns 21-56% GM — Akal Academy 29.01%, Kalgidhar Trust 27.15%, Akal Catering Mess 23.12%, De-Addiction Ward 24.85%, Eternal University 28.47%, Akal Hospital 31.01%, Nursing College 24.13%, Apple A Day 21.08%, Gurmat Camp 56.29%, University Students 41.18%. Campus institutional in aggregate: Rs 36.77 L costable revenue, Rs 26.39 L COGS, Rs 10.38 L gross profit, 28.23% — ABOVE the note's own retail 24.53%. The note never states a single campus-account margin. A reader acting on the title and conclusion would deprioritise ARY's #2 customer, which out-earns the retail counter.
refuted.correctedNumber: Campus institutional (10 accounts) Rs 51.25 L billed / Rs 36.77 L costable at 28.23% GM = Rs 10.38 L gross profit. Only Hunger Heroes earns nothing.

refuted.claim: Hunger Heroes: 12 bills, Rs 69.81 L revenue, Rs 69.10 L COGS, Rs 0.72 L GP, 1.03% GM (headline, table, and 'twelve bills a year averaging Rs 5.82 lakh')
refuted.why: Every figure reproduces to the rupee on the printed SQL (rev 6,981,332.03; cogs 6,909,510.89; gp 71,821.15; 1.0287%) — but it silently includes a bill this same vault flagged as a probable double-key the day before. 04-findings/Duplicate-Bill.md documents serials 2002751.0001 and 2002752.0001, both Rs 5,91,370.12 on the same 59 lines, keyed one minute apart (18:54 / 18:56 on 2026-05-11), no offsetting sale return. I confirmed the pair live. The rewrite never mentions it, never links [[Duplicate-Bill]] — even though Duplicate-Bill.md's only 'See also' points AT [[Institutional]]. Excluding 2002752.0001: 11 bills, Rs 63,89,962 revenue, Rs 63,12,323 COGS, Rs 77,639 GP, 1.215% GM.
refuted.correctedNumber: 11 real bills, Rs 63.90 L revenue, Rs 0.78 L GP, 1.22% GM, avg bill Rs 5.81 L (12th bill is a probable Rs 5.91 L duplicate)

refuted.claim: 'The one defensible institutional action... the 15 below-cost lines to Hunger Heroes — Rs 15.10 L of revenue losing Rs 1.08 L. Repricing those to zero margin recovers Rs 1.08 lakh with no new SKU, no capital and no conversation about volume.'
refuted.why: Three separate failures. (a) Duplicate contamination: ex-2002752.0001 the below-cost block is Rs 13.17 L of revenue losing Rs 0.92 L, not Rs 15.10 L / Rs 1.08 L. (b) Already fixed: I pulled last-sale dates on all 15. Ten of them — Rs 87,542 of the Rs 1,08,229, i.e. 81% — last transacted on 2026-05-11, and Rs 68,153 of that is Loose Milk, which the note ITSELF says stopped in May and moved to Milk_Z at +2.08% in June. You cannot 'recover' a loss the shop already stopped taking. Only seven SKUs appear on the current 2026-08-03 bill (Dahi_Z -9,792, Pumpkin_Z -5,344, Mausambi_Z -2,760, Ginger_Z -1,796, Paneer_Z -563, Golden Apple_Z -391, Mix Dal_L -40) = Rs 20,686 of live bleed. (c) 'No conversation' is false on the note's own evidence — repricing a named credit customer requires telling them, and the note says two paragraphs earlier that ARY 'has never quoted' a normal margin and nobody knows whether the Trust would pay one.
refuted.correctedNumber: ~Rs 0.21 L/yr of live below-cost bleed on SKUs still transacting; Rs 0.68 L of the Rs 1.08 L is the Loose Milk line already stopped in May 2026

refuted.claim: Retail (00001): 361,017 bills, Revenue Rs 479.24 L, COGS Rs 361.66 L, GP Rs 117.58 L, 24.53% — VERIFIED
refuted.why: The margin arithmetic reproduces exactly (47,924,017.13 / 36,166,383.55 / 24.535%), but the row mixes two scopes and the 'Revenue' column is mislabelled. Retail's actual 12m revenue is Rs 566.06 L on Qty*SaleRate (Rs 565.49 L on BillAmount); Rs 479.24 L is only the 84.7% of it that has a purchase-ledger cost. The 361,017 bill count is the FULL retail bill count — only 315,119 of those bills carry a costable line. The exclusion is also asymmetric across the table: retail loses 15.3% of its revenue to the WAC join, other-named 29.5%, Hunger Heroes and Katebaa 0%. Net effect: the four rows sum to Rs 6.45 Cr against a shop that turned Rs 7.68 Cr, and the missing Rs 1.23 Cr is never mentioned. The word 'costable' appears once, in a sentence below the table, and never in the table.
refuted.correctedNumber: Retail revenue Rs 566.06 L; Rs 479.24 L is the costable 84.7%; 315,119 bills carry a costable line. Rs 1.23 Cr (16%) of shop revenue is dropped from the table without disclosure.

refuted.claim: 'Every rupee moved from the retail counter to this channel destroys about 23 paise of margin.'
refuted.why: Computed on the gross basis the note itself declares unfair one paragraph later ('The table above therefore flatters retail and is fair to Hunger Heroes'). On the note's own like-for-like ex-tax numbers the spread is 13.98% - 0.43% = 13.55 pp, i.e. ~14 paise, not 23. Separately the claim assumes fungibility that does not exist: Hunger Heroes takes 9,800 kg of Rice 1 Kg, 12,500 kg of Atta and 13,605 L of loose milk in 12 documents — nothing about a 998-bill/day campus counter absorbs that volume, and the note offers no counterfactual.
refuted.correctedNumber: ~14 paise on the note's own preferred (ex-tax) basis; the transfer is not demonstrated to be fungible with retail at all

refuted.claim: Conclusion: 'The same effort spent on the 3,051 retail SKUs that are out of stock today works on a 24.53% base.'
refuted.why: Internal contradiction. The note's own ex-tax section restates walk-in retail to 13.98% and says the 24.53% figure 'flatters retail'. The recommendation then sizes the alternative prize on the flattering number it just disowned — nearly doubling the implied payoff of the availability programme. If 13.98% is right the note should use it; if it is not right the ex-tax table should not be published as VERIFIED. It cannot have both.
refuted.correctedNumber: 13.98% on the note's own ex-tax basis (Rs 420.44 L revenue, Rs 361.66 L COGS)

refuted.claim: Eternal University: Rs 99,483.50 in 12m, of which Rs 3,709 is edible oil (VERIFIED — two Jivo 5-litre packs), Rs 20,987 stoles, Rs 12,250 kurtis, Rs 10,575 curtains, Rs 9,584 trousers and shirts
refuted.why: The account total (Rs 99,483.50), kurtis (Tejoo Kurti 3 Pc Set Rs 12,250), curtains (Rs 5,985 + Rs 4,590 = Rs 10,575) and trousers/shirts (Pr Trouser Rs 5,592 + Raja Shirt Fs 1 Rs 3,992 = Rs 9,584) all reproduce exactly. Two descriptors do not. 'Two Jivo 5-litre packs' is wrong: Rs 3,709 is FOUR units across TWO SKUs — 3 x Jivo Mustard Oil 5 Ltr (Rs 2,759) + 1 x Jivo Canola Oil 5 Ltr Cold Press (Rs 950). It also excludes Loose Desi Ghee Rs 2,000 and Minchy's Kachi Ghani 500 Ml Rs 100, so edible fats on this account are Rs 5,809, not Rs 3,709. 'Rs 20,987 of stoles' only reaches that total by counting Db Lohi Rs 1,099, which is a lohi, not a stole; the two stole SKUs total Rs 19,888. These are rhetorical props in the section that carries the whole 'EU does not buy food' argument.
refuted.correctedNumber: Rs 3,709 = 4 packs across 2 SKUs (3 mustard + 1 canola); edible fats Rs 5,809; stoles Rs 19,888

refuted.claim: 'The campus mess buys Rs 25,845 of staples from ARY in a year — Rs 2,154 a month' (and Akal Catering Services provisions Rs 0.26 L, VERIFIED)
refuted.why: Stated to the rupee as VERIFIED with no query, and I cannot land on it from the note's own stated basket. Using the note's definition of provisions — 'grain, flour, pulses, dairy, veg, oil, tea, spices, sugar' — account 0000A totals Rs 21,395 (Spices 11,810 + Tea & Coffee 4,199 + Salt & Sugar 3,100 + Atta 1,310 + Vegetable 586 + Pulses 280 + Rice 70 + Oil & Ghee 40). Adding Dry Fruits gives Rs 27,244; adding General Items gives Rs 35,885. No combination reaches Rs 25,845. The conclusion (a mess that buys ~Rs 2k/month of staples) is unaffected, but the precision is not defensible and the classification is unpublished.
refuted.correctedNumber: Rs 21,395 on the note's own stated basket (Rs 1,783/month); the Rs 25,845 basket is undisclosed

refuted.claim: 'There is no unserved institutional food market here' (from the Local Creditors table)
refuted.why: Unlabelled inference presented as a finding, and the evidence does not carry it. The ledger proves only that ARY has BOUGHT Rs 4.72 L from four campus units since 2026-06-03 — three months of purchases. It says nothing about the size of campus institutional food demand, who else serves it, or whether it is served at all. The note contradicts itself two sections later under 'What this does NOT show': 'Any measure of campus food spend. ARY's ledger sees only what ARY billed.' Both cannot be true.

refuted.claim: 'it consumes the buying, the counter and the working capital of a Rs 7.68 Cr shop to produce Rs 0.72 lakh'
refuted.why: Rs 7.68 Cr checks out (SUM(Quantity*SaleRate) all customers 12m = Rs 7,68,20,329). The operational-load claim does not: this customer is 12 documents a year at one warehouse (16, Basement), against 373,461 bills shop-wide. No picking hours, no counter time, no credit days and no capital figure are measured anywhere in the note. The working-capital point is the one that might hold — bills average Rs 5.8 L on credit — but it is asserted, not sized.

refuted.claim: 'Every campus body ARY bills buys uniform cloth, winter wear and tuck-shop snacks, not provisions'
refuted.why: Overstated by the note's own table, which puts mess provisions at Rs 6.17 L / 12.0% of the ten accounts, and Akal Academy alone at Rs 2.12 L. 'Not provisions' reads as zero; 12% is not zero. It also does not hold body-by-body: University Students (Rs 5.16 L) is 100% apparel, but De-Addiction Ward is Confectionery/Fruits/Personal Care and Akal Academy carries Oil & Ghee Rs 1.16 L and Fruits Rs 1.30 L.
refuted.correctedNumber: Provisions are 12.0% (Rs 6.17 L) of the ten campus accounts, not nil

missing: The margin of the campus institution accounts. The note collects Rs 51.25 L of campus revenue and never costs it. It is 28.23% — better than retail. Without that row the note's title, headline and conclusion all point the reader the wrong way.

Any mention of, or link to, 04-findings/Duplicate-Bill.md. That note flags a Rs 5,91,370.12 double-key on THIS customer, was written the day before, and its only 'See also' is [[Institutional]]. Every Hunger Heroes number in this rewrite carries it. Worse, Duplicate-Bill.md still says 'the customer is the langar feeding programme' — a claim the verify pass refuted — and the rewrite left that standing at the exact link that points back at it.

That Hunger Heroes is ACCELERATING, which is what makes the finding urgent. Bill dates: Sep, Oct, Dec 2025, then four on 11-May-2026, then Jun 23 / Jun 26 / Jun 29 / Jul 21 / Aug 3. Eight of twelve bills fall in the last four months; the Jun-Aug run rate is ~Rs 28 L a quarter, ~Rs 110 L annualised against Rs 69.81 L trailing. The note's caveat ('a stopped customer and a lumpy one look the same') reads as though it might have stopped. It has not.

A reconciliation. The four channel rows sum to Rs 6.45 Cr; the shop turned Rs 7.68 Cr. Rs 1.23 Cr of revenue has no purchase-ledger cost and is dropped without a word. A reader adding the column will not be able to make it balance.

The coverage rate per channel, which is what makes the comparison unfair rather than merely incomplete: retail is costed on 84.7% of its revenue, other-named on 70.5%, Hunger Heroes and Katebaa on 100%. The note discloses full coverage for HH ('all 96 SKUs') and stays silent on retail's.

The queries behind the Rs 25.52 L / Rs 19.56 L / Rs 6.17 L composition split and the Rs 25,845 mess-staples figure. Every other table in the note prints or implies its SQL; these two — the ones whose classification is a judgment call — do not, and the mess figure does not reproduce from the basket the note itself defines.
